newsitem.title: USA: Marcus plans private debt placement.
newsitem.headline: Marcus plans private debt placement.

text.p: Marcus Corp, which operates motels, movie theaters, hotels, resorts, and restaurants, said Tuesday it plans a $200 million private placement of long-term debt over the next 30 days.
The private placement will include an initial draw of about $50 million on or about October 1, 1996.
"The funds will be used to carry out our growth strategy in all four divisions, " Stephen Marcus, chairman, said in a statement.

On September 16, Marcus reported earnings for its first quarter ended August 22, 1996 of $0.59 a share, compared with year-ago earnings of $0.53 before a $0.75 gain from the sale of restaurants. Including the gain, the year-ago earnings were $1.28 a share.

Marcus said the company's movie theater division experienced a late-summer softness due to the impact of the Olympic Games in Atlanta on movie attendance. He added that the divison added 47 new screens during the quarter and another 39 screens are under construction or in development.

Revenues and earnings for the Budgetel Inns were up for the quarter, but occupancy rates have softened slightly. "We are beginning to see signs that the mid-price economy lodging segment is becoming overbuilt in certain areas," he said.
A significant number of competitive new properties have opened during the past 90 days with more under construction, which could place pressure on operating margins, he said.

Should this trend continue, Marcus said it believes good acquisition opportunities may develop. The division's goal of operating and franchising 300 Budgetel Inns by the year 2000 is unchanged, he added.

Marcus said its hotels and resorts division generated higher revenues and earnings for the quarter, despite unseasonably cold weather in early summer which delayed the opening of its Grand Geneva Resort & Spa's Highlands golf course until August. Plans are under way for the renovation of its Erawan Garden Resort in Indian Wells, California, which the division acquired in August. The resort is expected to reopen in fall 1997 under a new name.

The company's KFC restaurants had a very strong quarter, continuing an upward trend in revenues and earnings, it said. Results benefited from new product rollouts and increased sales through its home delivery program, Marcus said. The company said it plans to open its first converted two-in-one KFC/Taco Bell unit during the third quarter.
Marcus shares are currently trading off 3/8 to 23-1/2.
